claims.claim: Winter was snowy, which gave good soil water and an early growth cycle.
Summer was hot and nearly rainless from mid-June. Water stress raised sugars and polyphenols.
claims.quote: The lack of water put a tremendous strain on the vines
claims.note: Two sources agree. Quote is from the Wine Scholar Guild.

claims.claim: Frost, hail and flowering were not described in any source read.
Ripening and harvest came about 10 days early. Grapes were healthy and aromatic, needing little intervention.
Yields were down about 10% in the Wine Scholar Guild chart. Beverfood calls 2015 a record year for both quality and quantity. Nearly 14 million bottles of Amarone were reported for 2015.
Rain above average earlier in the year was reported to raise humidity during drying, with only a touch of botrytis that producers controlled. Picking for drying began at the end of September.
claims.note: Single search summary attributed to the Wine Scholar Guild. Not found on the chart page when read. Treat as unverified.

claims.claim: Amarone is ripe and stylish with deep colour, vigorous tannins and intense dark fruit. Not as rich as the best years, with 12 to 15 years of ageing potential.
Acidity dropped in the heat, so wines are softer and rounder, with ripe cherry and wild berry fruit and a pleasant tannic texture.
Italy's Finest Wines gives 2015 five stars and calls it exceptional. This is a third-party chart, not the Consorzio.

conflicts: Yields: Wine Scholar Guild says quantity was down about 10%. Beverfood describes the vintage as a record for quantity. Possibly different scopes (grape volume versus bottles of Amarone). Unresolved.

Season: Italy's Finest Wines says a snowy winter and early start with healthy fruit. Vogadori calls it a season of extreme temperatures with little safety. Treat as a hot, demanding year with a good outcome.
gaps: No Consorzio Tutela Vini Valpolicella vintage rating or official harvest report was found or read.
Drying conditions that autumn and winter not found in a source read in full.

sheet.vintage: 2015 was a hot, dry summer and an early harvest. The Amarone is ripe, soft and rounder than the great years.
